criteria.detail: 7 of 8 ACs fully implemented; AC-007 exists only at the data layer.
100% by tool; AC-007 is covered at the data layer only, not the UI layer.
One feature on the shared branch.
Retry bound measured by driving real mutations; escaping tested with a hostile payload.
Production audit clean; escaped interpolation; one recipient per send; no credential exposure.
Test report and plan match the implementation.
NFR-001/003/004 tested; AC-001 timing is unverified because no provider exists in tests.
AC-007 unmet and AC-001 timing unverified.

findings.issue: No per-registration delivery view: listLifecycleDeliveries exists and is tested, but the admin sees only aggregate counts and failures.
AC-001 promises a confirmation within 60 seconds but only scheduling is proven; delivery timing is untested because no provider is configured.
The send path is exercised only up to the dispatch boundary in tests.

security.reason: Production dependency audit is clean (0 vulnerabilities with --omit=dev). Template interpolation is escaped, each send has exactly one recipient, and provider credentials stay server-side. The preference mutation is scoped to the caller's own registrations.

baseline.detail: setEmailPreference only patches registrations owned by the caller.
No new public submission surface; dispatch is internal.
All new functions take validated args.
Every interpolated value is escaped before it reaches the HTML body.
Provider credentials remain in environment variables.

performance.reason: The confirmation is scheduled rather than awaited, so provider latency never reaches the registration mutation; sweeps are bounded to 100 items per run and read through an index.
performance.method: Code review of the dispatch path plus the sweep bounds; no runtime measurement applicable.

nfr.target: confirmation is transactional, optional email honours the preference
registration latency independent of the provider
